```{r scm-define}
# ── Structural Causal Model (SCM) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The SCM formalises the trimmed directed graph as a set of structural
# equations with explicit noise terms. Each equation is:
#
#   X_i = f_i(pa(X_i)) + ε_i
#
# where f_i is linear with lavaan standardised coefficients, and ε_i is
# Gaussian with SD = sqrt(1 - R²_i), calibrated so that each variable
# has variance ≈ 1 on the standardised scale.
#
# Exogenous variable:
#   politics ~ N(0, 1)
#
# Endogenous variables (in topological order):
#   belief_concern    = β_pol_bc  * politics + ε_bc
#   harm_future       = β_bc_hf   * belief_concern + ε_hf
#   trust_science     = β_bc_ts   * belief_concern + ε_ts
#   harm_present      = β_hf_hp   * harm_future
#                     + β_bc_hp   * belief_concern + ε_hp
#   policy_support    = β_ts_ps   * trust_science
#                     + β_bc_ps   * belief_concern
#                     + β_pol_ps  * politics + ε_ps
#   weather_risk_prep = β_hp_wr   * harm_present + ε_wr
#   social_norms      = β_ts_sn   * trust_science
#                     + β_ps_sn   * policy_support + ε_sn
#   climate_behavior  = β_hp_cb   * harm_present
#                     + β_wr_cb   * weather_risk_prep
#                     + β_sn_cb   * social_norms + ε_cb
#
# Intervention via do(X = v): replace X's structural equation with X = v,
# a constant. All downstream nodes are updated; upstream nodes are unchanged.

# ── Path coefficients (from lavaan standardised solution) ─────────────────────
scm_coefs <- list(
  pol_bc  = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "politics"          & std_tr$To == "belief_concern"],
  bc_hf   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "belief_concern"    & std_tr$To == "harm_future"],
  bc_ts   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "belief_concern"    & std_tr$To == "trust_science"],
  hf_hp   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "harm_future"       & std_tr$To == "harm_present"],
  bc_hp   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "belief_concern"    & std_tr$To == "harm_present"],
  ts_ps   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "trust_science"     & std_tr$To == "policy_support"],
  bc_ps   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "belief_concern"    & std_tr$To == "policy_support"],
  pol_ps  = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "politics"          & std_tr$To == "policy_support"],
  hp_wr   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "harm_present"      & std_tr$To == "weather_risk_prep"],
  ts_sn   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "trust_science"     & std_tr$To == "social_norms"],
  ps_sn   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "policy_support"    & std_tr$To == "social_norms"],
  hp_cb   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "harm_present"      & std_tr$To == "climate_behavior"],
  wr_cb   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "weather_risk_prep" & std_tr$To == "climate_behavior"],
  sn_cb   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "social_norms"      & std_tr$To == "climate_behavior"],
  hf_ts   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "harm_future"       & std_tr$To == "trust_science"],
  bc_wr   = std_tr$Beta[std_tr$From == "belief_concern"    & std_tr$To == "weather_risk_prep"]
)

# Verify all coefficients found
cat("SCM path coefficients:\n")
purrr::iwalk(scm_coefs, ~cat(sprintf("  %-10s  %.3f\n", .y, .x)))
stopifnot(all(sapply(scm_coefs, length) == 1))

# ── Residual SDs from the same lavaan working SCM ─────────────────────────────
# Use equation-level R² from the simultaneous lavaan model, not from the
# separate lm() diagnostics, so the SCM is parameterized from one coherent fit.

r2_lav <- lavaan::lavInspect(sem_fit_tr, "rsquare")

# Make sure all endogenous nodes are represented
print(round(r2_lav, 3))

scm_resid_sd <- c(
  politics          = 1.000,  # exogenous root node on standardized scale
  belief_concern    = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["belief_concern"])),
  harm_future       = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["harm_future"])),
  trust_science     = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["trust_science"])),
  harm_present      = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["harm_present"])),
  policy_support    = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["policy_support"])),
  weather_risk_prep = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["weather_risk_prep"])),
  social_norms      = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["social_norms"])),
  climate_behavior  = sqrt(1 - unname(r2_lav["climate_behavior"]))
)

cat("Residual SDs from lavaan working SCM:\n")
print(round(scm_resid_sd, 3))


# ── Core SCM simulation function ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# n:        number of simulated individuals
# intervene: named list of hard interventions, e.g. list(harm_present = 0.5)
#            do(X = v) replaces X's structural equation with X = v for all n
# seed:     for reproducibility

simulate_scm <- function(n = 10000,
                         intervene = list(),
                         seed      = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  p <- scm_coefs

  # Helper: draw noise or zeros for pinned nodes
  noise <- function(node, n) {
    if (node %in% names(intervene)) rep(0, n)
    else rnorm(n, 0, scm_resid_sd[node])
  }

  # Helper: pin or compute
  pin <- function(node, expr) {
    if (node %in% names(intervene)) rep(intervene[[node]], n)
    else expr
  }

  # Topological order
  pol  <- pin("politics",
              rnorm(n, 0, scm_resid_sd["politics"]))

  bc   <- pin("belief_concern",
              p$pol_bc * pol + noise("belief_concern", n))

  hf   <- pin("harm_future",
              p$bc_hf * bc + noise("harm_future", n))

  ts   <- pin("trust_science",
              p$bc_ts * bc + p$hf_ts * hf + noise("trust_science", n))

  hp   <- pin("harm_present",
              p$hf_hp * hf + p$bc_hp * bc + noise("harm_present", n))

  ps   <- pin("policy_support",
              p$ts_ps * ts + p$bc_ps * bc + p$pol_ps * pol +
                noise("policy_support", n))

  wr   <- pin("weather_risk_prep",
              p$hp_wr * hp + p$bc_wr * bc + noise("weather_risk_prep", n))

  sn   <- pin("social_norms",
              p$ts_sn * ts + p$ps_sn * ps + noise("social_norms", n))

  cb   <- pin("climate_behavior",
              p$hp_cb * hp + p$wr_cb * wr + p$sn_cb * sn +
                noise("climate_behavior", n))

  tibble::tibble(
    politics          = pol,
    belief_concern    = bc,
    harm_future       = hf,
    trust_science     = ts,
    harm_present      = hp,
    policy_support    = ps,
    weather_risk_prep = wr,
    social_norms      = sn,
    climate_behavior  = cb
  )
}

# ── Verify model: simulated marginal SDs should be close to 1 ─────────────────
obs_baseline <- simulate_scm(n = 50000)
cat("\nSimulated marginal SDs (should be ≈ 1.0 for standardised model):\n")
print(round(apply(obs_baseline, 2, sd), 3))

cat("\nSimulated marginal means (should be ≈ 0):\n")
print(round(apply(obs_baseline, 2, mean), 3))

cat("\nSimulated CB mean:", round(mean(obs_baseline$climate_behavior), 4), "\n")
cat("Simulated CB SD:  ", round(sd(obs_baseline$climate_behavior),   4), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 8. Intervention Simulation

This section asks two related questions. First, does the directional structure identified in Section 7 actually change the conclusions relative to a naive undirected reading of the GGM? Second, given the directed model, which attitude nodes have the most leverage over downstream climate behavior? The two subsections address these in order: the GGM–SCM comparison motivates why directionality matters, and the SCM intervention ranking shows what it implies for behavior change.

## 8.1 Directed vs undirected: why directionality matters

The GGM and the SCM describe the same system but answer different questions. The GGM is undirected: conditioning on a node updates all connected nodes symmetrically via the multivariate normal conditional expectation, with no notion of upstream or downstream. The SCM is directed: a do-operator intervention on a node only propagates to its descendants, leaving upstream nodes unchanged. The comparison below fixes `belief_concern` to +0.5 SD under both models and shows where the two diverge — including the effect on the primary outcome `climate_behavior`.

```{r ggm-scm-comparison, fig.height=6, fig.width=9}
library(MASS)

# ── Use extended network which includes climate_behavior ──────────────────────
sigma_ggm <- cov(df_net_ext)
ggm_nodes <- extended_nodes

condition_ggm <- function(n, sigma, node_names, fixed = list(), seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  p <- length(node_names)

  if (length(fixed) == 0) {
    sims <- MASS::mvrnorm(n, mu = rep(0, p), Sigma = sigma)
    colnames(sims) <- node_names
    return(as.data.frame(sims))
  }

  fixed_idx  <- match(names(fixed), node_names)
  free_idx   <- setdiff(seq_len(p), fixed_idx)
  x_a        <- unlist(fixed)
  sigma_bb   <- sigma[free_idx,  free_idx,  drop = FALSE]
  sigma_ba   <- sigma[free_idx,  fixed_idx, drop = FALSE]
  sigma_aa   <- sigma[fixed_idx, fixed_idx, drop = FALSE]
  mu_cond    <- as.vector(sigma_ba %*% solve(sigma_aa) %*% x_a)
  sigma_cond <- sigma_bb - sigma_ba %*% solve(sigma_aa) %*% t(sigma_ba)
  free_sims  <- MASS::mvrnorm(n, mu = mu_cond, Sigma = sigma_cond)
  result     <- matrix(NA, nrow = n, ncol = p)
  colnames(result) <- node_names
  result[, free_idx]  <- free_sims
  result[, fixed_idx] <- matrix(
    x_a, nrow = n, ncol = length(fixed_idx), byrow = TRUE)
  as.data.frame(result)
}

N_COMP     <- 50000
fixed_node <- list(belief_concern = 0.5)

ggm_base <- condition_ggm(N_COMP, sigma_ggm, ggm_nodes,
                           fixed = list(),     seed = 42)
ggm_cond <- condition_ggm(N_COMP, sigma_ggm, ggm_nodes,
                           fixed = fixed_node, seed = 42)
scm_base <- simulate_scm(n = N_COMP, intervene = list(),     seed = 42)
scm_intv <- simulate_scm(n = N_COMP, intervene = fixed_node, seed = 42)

target_nodes <- setdiff(ggm_nodes, "belief_concern")

node_labels_short <- c(
  harm_present      = "Present Harm",
  harm_future       = "Future Harm",
  policy_support    = "Policy Support",
  trust_science     = "Trust Science",
  social_norms      = "Social Norms",
  politics          = "Politics",
  weather_risk_prep = "Weather Risk",
  climate_behavior  = "Climate Behavior"
)

node_level_order <- node_labels_short[c(
  "politics",
  "social_norms", 
  "policy_support",
  "trust_science",
  "weather_risk_prep",
  "harm_present",
  "harm_future",
  "climate_behavior"
)]

compare_df <- tibble::tibble(
  node  = rep(target_nodes, 2),
  shift = c(
    sapply(target_nodes,
           function(nd) mean(ggm_cond[[nd]]) - mean(ggm_base[[nd]])),
    sapply(target_nodes,
           function(nd) mean(scm_intv[[nd]]) - mean(scm_base[[nd]]))
  ),
  model = rep(c("GGM (conditioning)", "SCM (do-operator)"),
              each = length(target_nodes))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    node = factor(node_labels_short[node], levels = node_level_order)
  )

# ── y-axis label data — built from compare_df so factor levels align ──────────
ylabel_df <- compare_df |>
  dplyr::distinct(node)

ggplot2::ggplot(compare_df,
  ggplot2::aes(x = shift, y = node, colour = model, shape = model)) +
  # ── Climate Behavior row highlight ───────────────────────────────────────────
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    data = data.frame(
      node = factor("Climate Behavior", levels = levels(compare_df$node))
    ),
    aes(x = 0, xend = 0.60, y = node, yend = node),
    colour = "#E59866", linewidth = 15, alpha = 0.1,
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey60") +
  # ── y labels split by colour to avoid scale_colour_manual conflict ───────────
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = dplyr::filter(ylabel_df,
                         !node %in% c("Climate Behavior", "Politics")),
    aes(x = -0.02, y = node, label = node),
    hjust = 1, size = 3.5, colour = "black",
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = dplyr::filter(ylabel_df, node == "Climate Behavior"),
    aes(x = -0.02, y = node, label = node),
    hjust = 1, size = 3.5, colour = "#C06010", fontface = "bold",
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = dplyr::filter(ylabel_df, node == "Politics"),
    aes(x = -0.02, y = node, label = node),
    hjust = 1, size = 3.5, colour = "grey45", fontface = "bold",
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # ── inline annotations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = data.frame(
      node  = factor("Politics", levels = levels(compare_df$node)),
      shift = 0.01,
      model = "GGM (conditioning)"
    ),
    aes(x = shift, y = node,
        label = "Upstream — unchanged under do()"),
    hjust = 0, vjust = -0.8,
    size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic",
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = data.frame(
      node  = factor("Climate Behavior", levels = levels(compare_df$node)),
      shift = 0.01,
      model = "GGM (conditioning)"
    ),
    aes(x = shift, y = node,
        label = "Primary outcome"),
    hjust = 0, vjust = -0.8,
    size = 2.8, colour = "#C06010", fontface = "italic",
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    size = 3.5,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("GGM (conditioning)" = "#2E86AB",
               "SCM (do-operator)"  = "#E55934"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("GGM (conditioning)" = 16,
               "SCM (do-operator)"  = 17),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x),
    limits = c(-0.15, 0.65),
    breaks = c(0, 0.20, 0.40, 0.60)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x        = "Mean shift from baseline (SD units)",
    y        = NULL,
    title    = "GGM conditioning vs SCM intervention: do(belief_concern = +0.5 SD)",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "GGM updates all connected nodes symmetrically; ",
      "SCM propagates only to downstream descendants. ",
      "N = ", scales::comma(N_COMP), " per model."
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    axis.text.y        = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    plot.title         = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle      = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9)
  )
```

Three patterns stand out. The most diagnostic is `politics`: under GGM conditioning it shifts by \~0.28 SD because the undirected model sees only that people high in belief/concern tend to be more liberal — a correlation that propagates symmetrically along the edge in both directions. Under the SCM do-operator it does not move at all, because politics is upstream of `belief_concern` in the causal graph and interventions do not propagate backwards. This single row illustrates the core limitation of the undirected model for intervention reasoning: it cannot distinguish correlation from causation, and it cannot respect the direction of influence.

The second pattern involves `weather_risk_prep`, where the GGM gives a noticeably larger shift (\~0.25 SD) than the SCM (\~0.19 SD). In the SCM, weather risk is downstream of `harm_present` rather than directly downstream of `belief_concern`, so the do-operator effect reaches it only through an additional causal step and arrives attenuated. The GGM, being undirected, sees the direct partial correlation between belief_concern and weather risk and updates it more strongly. This gap is a concrete example of how the assumed causal routing changes the implied magnitude of effect even when both models agree that an association exists.

The third pattern concerns the primary outcome. `climate_behavior` shifts by \~0.20 SD under the SCM but \~0.27 SD under GGM conditioning — the GGM gives a larger estimate. This is because the GGM conflates all correlated pathways simultaneously, including associations through `social_norms` and `policy_support` that are present in the data but whose causal links to behavior are weak in the working model. The SCM gives a more conservative estimate by tracing only the specific directed paths, which run primarily through `harm_present` and `weather_risk_prep`. The GGM therefore overestimates the behavioral reach of belief_concern relative to what the directed causal structure implies.

The meaningful disagreements are concentrated exactly where directionality matters most: at upstream boundary nodes, along indirect causal routes, and at the behavioral endpoint.

## 8.2 SCM intervention effects on climate behavior

Taking the directed model seriously, we now simulate the effect on `climate_behavior` of fixing each attitude node to +0.5 SD via the do-operator. Because the GGM comparison in 8.1 showed that directionality matters — both for which nodes move and by how much — these results cannot be read off the GGM edge weights directly. The SCM is needed to propagate effects correctly through the causal chain.

```{r intervention-simulation}
N_SIM <- 50000

scenarios <- list(
  baseline                = list(),
  harm_present            = list(harm_present      = 0.5),
  belief_concern          = list(belief_concern    = 0.5),
  weather_risk_prep       = list(weather_risk_prep = 0.5),
  social_norms            = list(social_norms      = 0.5),
  trust_science           = list(trust_science     = 0.5),
  policy_support          = list(policy_support    = 0.5),
  harm_present_plus_norms = list(harm_present      = 0.5,
                                 social_norms      = 0.5),
  belief_plus_harm        = list(belief_concern    = 0.5,
                                 harm_present      = 0.5),
  # 2026-09-05 ADDED: the ACTUAL best pair (of 15) and best triple (of 20),
  # found by exhaustively simulating all 41 possible targets in
  # r_patches/02_full_orientation_enumeration_v4.R (see
  # tables/supp_table_all_combo_interventions.csv) -- neither combo above
  # turns out to be the strongest; they rank #17 and #12 out of 41
  # respectively. Kept alongside them (not replacing) so the prose below can
  # show the actual comparison rather than silently swapping numbers.
  best_pair               = list(belief_concern    = 0.5,
                                 weather_risk_prep = 0.5),
  best_triple             = list(harm_present      = 0.5,
                                 weather_risk_prep = 0.5,
                                 social_norms      = 0.5)
)

sim_results <- purrr::imap_dfr(scenarios, function(intv, label) {
  dat <- simulate_scm(n = N_SIM, intervene = intv, seed = 42)
  tibble::tibble(
    scenario = label,
    cb       = dat$climate_behavior,
    hp       = dat$harm_present,
    sn       = dat$social_norms,
    wr       = dat$weather_risk_prep,
    bc       = dat$belief_concern,
    ts       = dat$trust_science,
    ps       = dat$policy_support
  )
})

baseline_mean <- mean(sim_results$cb[sim_results$scenario == "baseline"])
baseline_sd   <- sd(sim_results$cb[sim_results$scenario == "baseline"])

scenario_summary <- sim_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cb_mean = mean(cb),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ate     = cb_mean - baseline_mean,
    ate_pct = ate / baseline_sd * 100,
    group = dplyr::case_when(
      scenario %in% c("harm_present_plus_norms",
                      "belief_plus_harm",
                      "best_pair",
                      "best_triple")             ~ "Combined",
      scenario %in% c("harm_present",
                      "weather_risk_prep")        ~ "Harm pathway",
      scenario == "belief_concern"               ~ "Belief pathway",
      scenario == "social_norms"                 ~ "Norms pathway",
      scenario %in% c("trust_science",
                      "policy_support")           ~ "Policy / response",
      TRUE                                       ~ NA_character_
    ),
    label = dplyr::case_when(
      scenario == "harm_present"            ~ "do(Present harm = +0.5 SD)",
      scenario == "belief_concern"          ~ "do(Belief/concern = +0.5 SD)",
      scenario == "weather_risk_prep"       ~ "do(Weather risk = +0.5 SD)",
      scenario == "social_norms"            ~ "do(Social norms = +0.5 SD)",
      scenario == "trust_science"           ~ "do(Trust science = +0.5 SD)",
      scenario == "policy_support"          ~ "do(Policy support = +0.5 SD)",
      scenario == "harm_present_plus_norms" ~ "do(Present harm + Social norms)",
      scenario == "belief_plus_harm"        ~ "do(Belief/concern + Present harm)",
      scenario == "best_pair"               ~ "do(Belief/concern + Weather risk) [best pair, of 15]",
      scenario == "best_triple"             ~ "do(Present harm + Weather risk + Social norms) [best triple, of 20]",
      TRUE                                  ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(group)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(ate))

get_ate <- function(nm) scenario_summary$ate[scenario_summary$scenario == nm]
get_ate_pct <- function(nm) scenario_summary$ate_pct[scenario_summary$scenario == nm]

cat("Average treatment effects on climate_behavior (SD units):\n")
print(scenario_summary |>
  dplyr::select(label, ate, ate_pct) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))), n = 20)
```

```{r intervention-plot-ate, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=9}
scenario_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    label      = forcats::fct_reorder(label, ate),
    label_text = sprintf("+%.3f SD", ate)
  ) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = ate, y = label, fill = group)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = label_text, x = ate + 0.003),
    hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey50") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Harm pathway"      = "#E55934",
      "Belief pathway"    = "#2E86AB",
      "Norms pathway"     = "#9B5DE5",
      "Policy / response" = "#F7B731",
      "Combined"          = "#3BB273"
    ),
    name = "Intervention type"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2)),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x        = "Average treatment effect on climate behavior (SD units)",
    y        = NULL,
    title    = "Causal effect of do(X = +0.5 SD) on climate behavior",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Model-implied shifts propagated through working SCM ",
      "(N = ", scales::comma(N_SIM), " simulated individuals). ",
      "Effects are in standardised units relative to baseline SD."
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    plot.title         = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle      = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9)
  )
```

The ranking reveals a clear hierarchy of leverage points. The two largest single-node effects come from `harm_present` (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("harm_present"))` SD, \~`r sprintf("%.0f", get_ate_pct("harm_present"))`% of a baseline SD) and `belief_concern` (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("belief_concern"))` SD, \~`r sprintf("%.0f", get_ate_pct("belief_concern"))`%), which are nearly identical in magnitude. `belief_concern` achieves this not through a direct path to behavior — there is none — but through a strong indirect chain: belief/concern → harm_future → harm_present → climate_behavior. Because the two nodes share this downstream route, naively combining them is partly redundant: fixing `belief_concern` and `harm_present` together yields only `r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("belief_plus_harm"))` SD (\~`r sprintf("%.0f", get_ate_pct("belief_plus_harm"))`%) — less than the sum of their individual effects, and, once every possible combination is checked rather than assuming the two strongest single levers pair best, not even a top-ranked two-node scenario. The same is true of fixing `harm_present` and `social_norms` together (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("harm_present_plus_norms"))` SD, \~`r sprintf("%.0f", get_ate_pct("harm_present_plus_norms"))`%): a reasonable-looking candidate on its own, but one that a full search shows is outperformed by several other combinations. `weather_risk_prep` has a meaningful but more modest single-node effect (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("weather_risk_prep"))` SD, \~`r sprintf("%.0f", get_ate_pct("weather_risk_prep"))`%), reflecting its direct path to `climate_behavior` but narrower upstream reach — it is downstream of `harm_present` and cannot be further amplified by fixing belief_concern.

To identify the actual best multi-node scenario rather than assuming it, we exhaustively simulated every possible combination of the six intervenable nodes — all 15 pairs and 20 triples, 41 targets in total, each re-simulated under all eight structural specifications from the orientation-uncertainty analysis in Section 3.4 (full results in Supplementary Table S-combo). The best two-node scenario is `belief_concern` + `weather_risk_prep` (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("best_pair"))` SD, \~`r sprintf("%.0f", get_ate_pct("best_pair"))`%), and the best three-node scenario — the single strongest target found among all 41 — is `harm_present` + `weather_risk_prep` + `social_norms` (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("best_triple"))` SD, \~`r sprintf("%.0f", get_ate_pct("best_triple"))`%). The pattern is intuitive in hindsight: `weather_risk_prep`'s own single-node effect is modest, but because it sits on a distinct, non-overlapping route to `climate_behavior`, pairing it with either of the two strongest single levers captures ground that pairing two nodes on the *same* pathway cannot. More generally, the most effective multi-node interventions in this causal structure combine levers from different causal pathways rather than doubling up on the two individually strongest nodes — a distinction only an exhaustive, structure-aware search surfaces.

The most policy-relevant finding is the disconnect between network connectivity and intervention leverage on the response side of the system. `policy_support` (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("policy_support"))` SD) and `trust_science` (`r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("trust_science"))` SD) are strongly connected within the attitude network, but fixing either one alone produces negligible shifts in `climate_behavior`. This is because both nodes sit on the trust/policy/norms branch of the causal graph whose only path to `climate_behavior` runs through `social_norms` with a small coefficient — and even fixing `social_norms` directly yields only `r sprintf("%+.3f", get_ate("social_norms"))` SD. Strong network edges do not automatically translate into behavioral leverage. The SCM makes this distinction visible in a way that the GGM alone cannot.

Results should be interpreted as model-implied scenario shifts under the assumed causal structure. The qualitative ordering of leverage points is more defensible than the precise numerical magnitudes, which depend on the specific path coefficients in the working SCM estimated on the wave-5 subsample (N = 870).
